To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnetic shielding effect of an iron sheath in MgB/sub2//Fe wires is due to the interaction between the iron and superconducting core, and that the effect of this interaction can be extended to higher fields by doping the MgB/sub2/ core with SiC.

(1) magnetic shielding in MgB2/Fe wires is very efficient, (2) the field dependence of the critical current of MgB2/ Fe wires can be improved by SiC doping, (3) at 10 K, Ic of SiC dopes wires increases with the field after an initial decrease and (4) the peak effect is extended to higher fields with the decrease of the temperature
(1) the magnetic shielding effect is not due to mere shielding by iron, and (2) the peak effect is not affected by the presence of the magnetic shielding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the magnetic properties of superconductors.
the study of the magnetic shielding effect in MgB/sub2//Fe superconductor wires and its influence on transport critical current.
the study of MgB/sub 3/Fe composite wires.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic shielding of the iron sheaths of MgB/sub 1/ wires is a strong effect that should be considered in any design of MgB/sub2//Fe superconductor for applications in magnetic fields.
magnetic shielding by iron sheath improves the critical current of MgB/sub 1/ wires at fields above 1 T.
magnetic shielding of MgB/sub 3/Fe wires can be achieved with a high degree of efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic shielding effect of iron on MgB/sub 3/ is not as strong as on NbTi, but the pinning enhancement due to iron is much stronger.
the magnetic properties of MgB/sub 1-x/Fe/sub x/ superconductor can be improved by the addition of iron.
the magnetic shielding effect of the iron sheaths is not the only effect that improves the performance of MgB/sub 1/ wires.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of iron sheath in MgB/sub2//Fe wires can significantly improve the performance of these wires, and that this improvement is independent of the presence of pinning centers.
the iron sheath is an effective way to improve the performance of MgB/sub 1/ wires at high fields.
the magnetic shielding effect in the MgB/sub2//Fe wires was not due to a magnetic field screening, but due to an interaction between MgB/sub  2/ and iron.
